Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

* A-1.2 Take a piece constituting the test sample. Lay it flat on a hori-

magnifying glass, the number of wales per decimetre of the fabric at six

IS : 3326 - 1978 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
COTTON STOCKINETTE 

( First Revision ) 



0. FOREWORD 

0*1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 13 February 1978, after the draft finalized by 
the Hosiery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile 
Division Council. 

0.2 Stockinette is a plain-knitted tubular cotton fabric. It is mainly used 
for cleaning machinery, particularly aircraft machinery and for wrap- 
ping meat. 

0.3 This standard was first published in 1965. The pH value of aqueous 
extract has been modified and the mass of fabric has been slightly 
lowered in the present revision. Also, the requirement in respect of 
dimensional change has been deleted since it has been found, during the 
implementation of the standard, that keeping the end use in view this 
requirement does not play any important role in judging the quality of 
the product. 

0.4 This standard is based on IND/AIR/TC/0555 (c) 'Specification for 
stockinette', issued by the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in 
this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of scoured cotton stocki- 
nette. 



♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ) . 

3 



IS : 3326 - 1978 

1.2 This standard does not prescribe the type of finish, feel, general 
appearance, etc, of the stockinette ( see also 3.2 ). 

2, MANUFACTURE 

2.1 Yarn — The cotton yarn used for knitting stockinette shall be sofr 
and evenly spun with 600 to 700 turns per metre. The approximate 
count shall be 20s (30 tex). 

2*2 Stockinette — The stockinette shall be plain-knitted and tubular in 
shape. It shall be well scoured and free from any filling material. It 
shall be reasonably free from manufacturing defects, such as large mends, 
ladders, dropped stitches, holes, cuts, tears and chemical damage. 

3. REQUIREMENTS 

3.1 The stockinette shall conform to the requirements as given in Table 1.

3.2 Sealed Sample — If, in order to illustrate or specify the indetermi- 
nable characteristics, such as type of finish, feel, general appearance, etc, 
a sample has been agreed upon and sealed, the supply shall be in 
conformity with the sample in such respects. 

3.2.1 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a matter of prior 
agreement between the buyer and the seller. 



IS : 3326 - 1978 

4. MARKING 

4.1 Each piece of stockinette shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark, if any; 

b) Length in metres of stockinette in a roll; 

c) Flat width in centimetres of stockinette; and 

d) Any other information as required by the buyer. 

4.2 BIS Certification Marking 

The product may also be marked with Standard Mark. 

4.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made 
thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of 
Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

5. PACKING 

5.1 Each piece of stockinette shall be made into a compact roll. A 
number of such rolls shall then be wrapped in kraft paper and packed in 
a bale in accordance with either IS : 3086-1965* or IS : 3325-1965f, as 
the case may be. 

6. SAMPLING 

6.1 Lot — The number of rolls of stockinette manufactured under similar 
conditions of production and delivered to a buyer against one despatch 
note shall constitute a lot. 

6.2 The conformity of the lot shall be determined on the basis of the 
tests carried out and the rolls selected from the lot. Unless otherwise 
agreed to between the buyer and the seller, the number of rolls to be 
selected at random shall be according to col 1 and 2 of Table 2.

APPENDIX A 

( Table 1 ) 

METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF WALES 
AND COURSES 



A-l. WALES 

A-l.l Take a piece constituting the test sample. Lay it flat on a hori- 
zontal surface (i^Note). Remove all creases and wrinkles without 
distorting the piece. Count with the help of a pick glass or magnifying 
glass the number of wales including any fraction on one side and similarly 
the number of wales including any fraction on the other side of the 
stockinette. Add the two values so obtained. 

Note — A board of 28 cm width and 50 cm length shall be inserted inside the 
tubular fabric, to facilitate counting of wales and courses of stockinette, which has a 
loose texture. 

A-2. COURSES 

A-2.1 Take a piece constituting the test sample. Lay it flat on a horizontal 
surface (see Note under A-l.l ). Remove all creases and wrinkles without 
distorting the piece. Count with the help of a pick glass or magnifying 
glass, the number of courses per decimetre of the fabric at five different 
places and calculate the average.
